cards.text: Paul, an apostle, is writing to the churches of Galatia (Gal 1:1-2). He just finished saying a person is justified by faith in Christ, not by works of the law (Gal 2:16). Now he turns to them, and friend, he does NOT warm up first: "O foolish Galatians! Who has bewitched you?"

cards.question: Paul reminds the Galatians of something they already saw. What was clearly portrayed before their very eyes?

cards.text: Then Paul says he'd like to learn just one thing from them. ONE thing. Every time somebody at work says "just one quick question," I clear my whole afternoon.

cards.question: Paul asks the Galatians if they received the Spirit by works of the law or by hearing with faith. True or false: Paul is pointing them to hearing with faith.

cards.text: And that one thing turns into another: "Are you so foolish? After starting in the Spirit, are you now finishing in the flesh?"

cards.question: Paul asks if the Galatians started in the Spirit and are now finishing in the flesh. What is he pointing out?

answers.text: They switched from how they started

cards.text: Picture me. An angel pulls me OUT of a junk drawer, and I climb right back in going, "Thanks, I'll finish this myself." Then Paul asks if they've suffered so much for nothing, if it really was for nothing.

cards.question: Paul asks about the Spirit again. Does God lavish His Spirit on the Galatians and do what among them because they practice the law?

cards.text: Then Paul goes ALL the way back to Abraham, the man God called to leave his country (Gen 12:1). Paul quotes the Scripture about him.

cards.question: Abraham ___ God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.
Paul tells the Galatians to understand what that means. Who does he say are the sons of Abraham?

answers.text: Those born in his family line

cards.text: Paul says the Scripture saw this coming. It foresaw that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, and it told Abraham the gospel ahead of time. That's not early, friend. That's EARLY early.

cards.question: The Scripture foretold the gospel to Abraham: all ___ will be blessed through you.
Paul wraps up his point about Abraham. True or false: he says those who keep the law are blessed along with Abraham, the man of faith.

cards.text: Now Paul flips the coin over. What about everybody who relies on works of the law?

cards.question: Paul says all who rely on works of the law are under what?

cards.text: And Paul doesn't just say it. He backs it up with what's written in the Law itself.

cards.question: Paul quotes the Law: cursed is everyone who does not continue to do how much of what's written in the Book of the Law?

cards.text: EVERYTHING. Not most of it. Not just on the good days. Friend, by the end on that counter I couldn't stamp ONE cookie straight, and that was my only job.

cards.question: Paul says no one is justified before God by the law, because the righteous will live by ___.

cards.text: Then Paul sets the law right next to faith and looks at how the law works.

cards.question: Paul compares the law and faith. True or false: he says the law is based on faith.

cards.text: The law runs on doing: "The man who does these things will live by them." But then Paul brings in the rescue from the curse.

cards.question: Who does Paul say redeemed us from the curse of the law?
How does Paul say Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law?

answers.text: By becoming a curse for us

cards.text: Paul quotes Scripture: "Cursed is everyone who is hung on a tree." Friend, he's talking about the cross. Jesus became that curse for us.

cards.question: Paul says Christ redeemed us so the blessing promised to Abraham would come to whom in Christ Jesus?
Christ redeemed us so that by ___ we might receive the promise of the ___.

findings.problem: Story card has three sentences: 'Then Paul says he'd like to learn just one thing from them.' / 'ONE thing.' / 'Every time somebody at work says...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question says the Galatians started in the Spirit, which rules out two wrong answers: 'They never really got started' and 'They started without the Spirit'. Only the right answer fits the question's own wording.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Story card has three sentences: 'Picture me.' / 'An angel pulls me OUT of a junk drawer...' / 'Then Paul asks...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't match the action of Galatians 3:3. Paul's point is starting in the Spirit and then trying to finish in the flesh. The image is climbing back into the drawer, which is going back to the dark, and 'I'll finish this myself' has nothing to finish inside a drawer. A stranger would say 'huh?'.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: In a letter, this asks the baker to guess a detail (work miracles, raise up judges or send prophets) instead of the meaning of Galatians 3:5. That is the same kind of question as the Psalm 23 'anoint his head with' bad example. The question also drops Paul's actual contrast, 'or because you hear and believe', which is never told on any card. Its wording also reads as if God does this because they practice the law.

rule.text: Ask about the movement and the meaning: what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says.

findings.problem: Story card has four sentences: 'Paul says the Scripture saw this coming.' / 'It foresaw...' / 'That's not early, friend.' / 'That's EARLY early.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card tells nothing new from the passage. It repeats card 4's answer ('EVERYTHING. Not most of it.') and adds a joke, so it works as a recap and doesn't move the passage forward. It also has four sentences.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
